title: rwst/Even-Integral
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib development of a paper, which improves on a problem by Dubickas. Dubickas (Glasgow Math. J. 48 (2006), 331–336) splits the reals α > 1 in two: α lies in 𝒵 when some real ξ ≠ 0 makes every integral part ⌊ξαⁿ⌋, n ≥ 1, even, and in 𝒮 otherwise. At α = 3/2 this is Mahler's question, and open; his Problem 5 asks whether 𝒮 has an element greater than 2. This formalization decides 𝒮 versus 𝒵 for every quadratic Pisot number: the golden mean is the only one in 𝒮, so none greater than 2 lies there and Problem 5 loses its whole natural class of candidates, though the problem itself stays open. The case that had resisted the source paper's four constructions is α = 1 + √2, settled by an exact computation rather than an estimate: with ξ = (2−√2)/4 one has ⌊ξ(1+√2)^(n+1)⌋ = Pₙ − [n odd] for the Pell numbers P, so every integral part is even. The mechanism generalizes: for a real quadratic pair with second conjugate in (−1,0), the closed-form multiplier ξ = −β/(α−β) makes m divide ⌊ξαⁿ⌋ for every n ≥ 0 whenever m ∣ a and m ∣ b−1 — an exact congruence, not a confinement of fractional parts — and all but finitely many of those integral parts are then composite. The informal account is the companion paper doi:10.13140/RG.2.2.20582.79689. Credit divides as follows, in contributor terms rather than bibliographic ones: the mathematical discovery and the formalization are the AI agent's; the agent also drafted the prose of the companion paper, which the author revised; the direction and the review are the author's, who is responsible for the mathematical content. Bibliographic authorship of the paper is the author's alone — the agent is credited in its Acknowledgements, not in its byline, as is usual for an AI tool. There is no sorry outside the deliberate placeholders in Challenge.lean, no project-defined axiom, no native_decide, and Mathlib is the only Lake dependency.
authors: Claude Code, claude-opus-5 (mathematical discovery, formalization, paper drafting)
